dossier.public_summary: This faint M-dwarf shows a shallow 12.6-day dip with a flat bottom and small size, but the dip is far deeper in some observations than in others. The depth changes by 113% between TESS sectors and by a factor of 15 among the four individual transits, with most of the signal coming from two unusually deep events. A consistent transiting planet should be the same depth every time, so variable-depth noise is the best explanation.
